tr.comment: The candidate addresses both parts of the prompt: whether everyone should learn English and whether local languages should be preserved. However, the final question ('how' to ensure their survival) is answered only cursorily with vague suggestions ('Schools and governments must do things'). Development of ideas remains at a straightforward B1 level.
tr.name: Task Response

cc.comment: The essay follows a clear four-paragraph layout (introduction, English benefits, local languages importance, conclusion). Cohesive devices are basic and occasionally repetitive ('However', 'Also', 'In conclusion', 'Without knowing English'). Referencing and transitions between sentences are sometimes mechanical.
cc.name: Coherence and Cohesion

lr.comment: Vocabulary is sufficient to convey general meaning on a familiar topic, but relies heavily on simple, repetitive terms ('important', 'lost', 'clever', 'people', 'good'). Collocation errors and unidiomatic word choices are present ('many knowledges', 'talk English', 'past times', 'musics', 'keep both languages living', 'our personality').
lr.name: Lexical Resource

gr.comment: Grammatical control is limited to basic structures with frequent systematic errors in subject-verb agreement ('many people speaks', 'They is', 'It make'), passive voice formation ('everyone should be learned English'), missing prepositions/determiners ('going other country', 'That’s reason', 'from internet and book'), and countable/uncountable noun distinction ('many knowledges', 'musics').
gr.name: Grammatical Range and Accuracy

tags.tr: English is very important today and taught in many schools since it helps to students with job and going other country. However, that local languagaes is not taught in schools is also big issue, because some local languages can get lost in future. I think everyone should be learned English since many people speaks it. For example, many companies look for workers who talk English. It is the global language. Also, if you know English, you can learn many knowledges from internet and book. That’s reason schools teach it. It make students more clever. English is also important because it allows people to travel and communicate with others from different countries. Without knowing English, it is difficult to connect with people around the world. But local languages are very serious too. They is part of culture and histories. If we lost them, we forget our past times. Some stories and musics is only in local language. It is very difficult to change them into English because they lose original meanings. Local languages also help people feel connected to their community and traditions. If we stop speaking these languages, we could lose important knowledge about our ancestors and history. In conclusion, English is good for job and learning, but we must not ignore local languages. They are our personality. Schools and governments must do things to keep both languages living, so we can protect culture and also grow in modern life.

tr_details.content: Schools and governments must do things to keep both languages living
tr_details.comment: The prompt asks 'if so, how?' to ensure language survival. Simply stating that authorities 'must do things' lacks development and concrete measures.
tr_details.revision: Schools and governments should implement bilingual curricula and fund cultural documentation programs to keep indigenous languages alive.
tr_details.combined_tagged: Schools and governments must do things to keep both languages living
